title: Semidefinite lifts of the perfect matching polytope
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that the shifted matching matrices, with entries |M ∩ δ(U)| − 1 + ρ for odd sets U and perfect matchings M of the complete graph K_n, have positive semidefinite rank 2^{Ω(n)} for every fixed 0 < ρ < 1, so that every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has exponential size. The first lesson develops PSD factorizations, a normalization of their traces, and the conic duality that turns a semidefinite lift into a PSD factorization of a matrix of slacks. The second proves the local averaging theorem for restrictions of cuts to a cell, with explicit constants, from a trace formula and a multiplicity bound for invariant subspaces. The third proves the orthogonal splitting inequality for finite families of positive semidefinite matrices. The fourth proves the Fourier smoothing theorem for product averages of positive semidefinite matrix functions through a fourth-order Gram potential. The fifth constructs expanding multigraphs and a functional that is nonnegative on low-degree squares and negative on the disagreement count of an odd parity system. The sixth realizes the parity system by odd cuts and perfect matchings and proves the lower bounds. The seventh proves a uniform smoothing theorem for averages over perfect matchings with prescribed numbers of edges between a fixed number of cells.
prerequisites: finite-dimensional linear algebra: the spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices
basic real analysis: compactness of closed bounded sets in finite dimensions, comparison of sums with integrals

course RT-FIN (Representations of finite groups), lessons The symmetric groups I: Young tableaux and Young symmetrizers (Theorem 4.3, Proposition 5.2 and the Young symmetrizer (5)) and The symmetric groups II: branching, Jucys-Murphy elements and Young's seminormal form (Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 4.3); used only in the seventh lesson

Differences of presentation, none a correction: the local averaging lemma is proved with the explicit constant theta_d(k) = 2^((d+10)/2) k^(-1/4) (1 + log k)^(1/2) for even k >= d + 16 kappa(kappa+1), kappa = d/4 + 1/2; the expander lemma is proved for every even t; the corollary on lifts is deduced from a conic duality lemma proved in the first lesson, which turns a lift of size r into a factorization of size r + 1, in place of the cone-factorization theorem of Gouveia, Parrilo and Thomas and Edmonds's facet description, which are cited as context only; the representation theory of the symmetric group in the seventh lesson is taken from the programme's RT-FIN lessons, with the one-row and one-column diagrams identified through the Young symmetrizer.
